interconnectors.name: Eastern Green Link 1 (Torness to Hawthorn Pit)

ai_summary:
Scotland’s generation fleet is demonstrating robust renewable output, with wind generation currently delivering 4.4 GW across the regional network. This surge in clean power has driven Scottish carbon intensity down to an impressive 32 gCO2/kWh, underscoring the dominant role of wind assets in displacing fossil-fuel generation. However, structural transmission limits continue to impede full asset utilization, as evidenced by the 221.1 MWh of wasted energy recorded over the current operating window.

This curtailment highlights persistent bottlenecks across critical export corridors, particularly the B6 boundary, where export capacity into southern demand centers remains saturated. As a consequence, the system operator is compelled to pay constraint payments to turn down Scottish wind while dispatching costlier, more carbon-intensive balancing units elsewhere on the Great Britain network. This friction inflates balancing mechanism costs and diminishes the carbon-abatement potential of the domestic fleet.

Mitigating this 221.1 MWh volume requires immediate focus on localized flexibility, including accelerated deployment of co-located battery storage and responsive demand-side management. Looking forward, sustained reinforcement of cross-border transmission infrastructure, notably planned subsea HVDC links, remains vital to unlocking stranded wind capacity, driving down system balancing expenses, and securing Scotland's trajectory toward sustained negative or near-zero operational emissions.
